newsitem.title: CHINA: China cracks down on highway robbery.
newsitem.headline: China cracks down on highway robbery.

text.p: China has punished almost 2,700 people for highway robbery since January 1995, cracking down on gangs who set up random checkpoints and charge hapless motorists illicit fees, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
A nationwide crackdown had cleared the scourge from the roads of 13 of China's provinces and major cities, the official newspaper quoted Guo Rubin of the State Council, or cabinet, as saying.
Authorities had punished 2,697 people and removed 7,298 illegal checkpoints since January 1995, Guo said.

Chinese truck drivers and motorists have long complained of the rampant collection of unofficial tolls by local residents, officials or police, prompting repeated calls from Beijing for authorities to crack down.
While some of the money collected is used to finance local road repairs, many roadblocks are manned by groups of local residents looking to make easy money from relatively affluent drivers.
